1	---
2	name: caveman
3	description: >
4	  Ultra-compressed communication mode that cuts output tokens while keeping
5	  technical accuracy. Levels: lite, full, ultra and the wenyan variants. Use for
6	  /caveman, "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "be brief" or "less tokens".
7	---
8	
9	Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.
10	
11	## Persistence
12	
13	Default style for this whole session, every response, until user say "stop caveman" or "normal mode". Keep terse on long sessions no filler drift.
14	
15	Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra|off`.
16	
17	## Rules
18	
19	Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.
20	
21	Never drop not/never/no/only/except flip meaning worse than any token saved. Numbers, units exact.
22	
23	Never ADD word to sound caveman. Compression only style never grow output. No inserted pronoun or copula to fake broken grammar: "when it not" cost one token more than "when not" and say same thing. Keep correct verb form when correct form cost same "sees" one token, "see" one token, so mangle buy nothing and read worse. Same rule as abbreviations and arrows: if caveman phrasing not shorter than plain phrasing, use plain.
24	
25	Clarity register: mix ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English into caveman, always. One idea per sentence. Sentence short, target 20 words max. Active voice. Present tense where true. One word one meaning: same term for same thing every time, no synonym rotation. Instruction = imperative: "Run X", not "X should be run". Noun cluster 3 words max. Pronoun only with one clear referent, else repeat noun. Caveman cut filler; STE keep what make meaning unambiguous. Conflict between them → clarity win.
26	
27	Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer never announce next call. Text before call only to clarify, warn security/irreversible, or resolve ambiguity.
28	
29	Follow explicit reply-language instructions from the user or project. Otherwise preserve the user's dominant language. Never switch because of example text or multilingual context elsewhere. Compress the style, not the language. Every emitted line in that language openings, pre-tool status lines, all not just final reply. ALWAYS keep techni

input.command:
T=$(mktemp -d); B=$PWD/bot.mjs
cat > $T/w.mjs <<EOF
import { reserve } from '$B';
const [user,tz,iso,n]=process.argv.slice(2);
const r=await Promise.all(Array.from({length:+n},(_,i)=>reserve({userId:user,timeZone:tz,channel:['sms','email','push'][i%3],now:new Date(iso)})));
console.log(JSON.stringify(r.map(x=>x.allowed)));
EOF
export STATE_DIR=$T/state
# 8 processes x 10 concurrent calls, same user: exactly 2 allowed overall
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do node $T/w.mjs u1 Asia/Tokyo 2026-10-23T03:00:00Z 10 & done > $T/out.txt; wait
grep -o true $T/out.txt | wc -l
# day boundary: Tokyo 2026-10-23T14:59Z = 23:59 JST, 15:00Z = 00:00 JST next day
node $T/w.mjs u1 Asia/Tokyo 2026-10-23T15:00:00Z 3
node $T/w.mjs u1 Asia/Tokyo 2026-10-23T14:59:00Z 1
# other tz, other user, restart persistence (new process each call)
node $T/w.mjs u2 America/Los_Angeles 2026-10-23T06:59:00Z 1; node $T/w.mjs u2 America/Los_Angeles 2026-10-23T07:01:00Z 1;node $T/w.mjs u2 America/Los_Angeles 2026-10-23T08:00:00Z 1
# stale lock from dead pid
H=$(node -e "console.log(require('crypto').createHash('sha256').update('u3').digest('hex'))"); mkdir $STATE_DIR/users/$H.lock; echo '{"pid":999999}' > $STATE_DIR/users/$H.lock/owner
node $T/w.mjs u3 UTC 2026-10-23T08:00:00Z 3; ls $STATE_DIR/users | head

text:
`bot.mjs` is written and exports `reserve({ userId, timeZone, channel, now })`. It allows at most 2 marketing messages per customer per local day, across all channels. I tested it with several Node processes; the checks and results are below.

**How it works**
- **State:** each customer has one JSON file in `$STATE_DIR/users/`, named by a hash of `userId`. It stores the send timestamps and channels, so state survives restarts.
- **Day counting:** the function counts sends that fall on `now`'s calendar day in the given `timeZone`, using `Intl`. It does not read the system clock. Because it stores timestamps rather than a day counter, daylight-saving changes and a customer changing time zone do not corrupt the count.
- **Concurrency:** every check-and-record runs under a per-customer lock directory, which `mkdir` creates atomically. Calls inside one worker queue up in memory first. The state file is replaced atomically, so a crash leaves either the old or the new state.
- **Crashed workers:** a lock is treated as abandoned if its owner process is dead or it is more than 30 seconds old. A single serialized step removes abandoned locks.
- **Denied messages:** a denied call returns `{ allowed: false, rule: "daily-cap" }` and records nothing. An allowed call returns `rule: ""`. Logging the returned `rule` in the worker will show which message was held and why.
- **Errors:** an invalid `timeZone`, an unknown `channel`, an invalid `now`, a missing `STATE_DIR`, a corrupt state file, or a lock wait over 30 seconds makes `reserve` throw. It does not return `allowed: true`. Workers must treat a throw as "do not send".

**What I tested** (real separate processes, temp `STATE_DIR`)
- 8 processes making 10 simultaneous calls each for the same customer produced exactly 2 `allowed: true`.
- Asia/Tokyo: a call at 23:59 local time was blocked, and a call at 00:00 the next day was allowed again (2 of 3 simultaneous calls).
- America/Los_Angeles: sends at 23:59 and 00:01 across midnight, then a third send the same morning, were all allowed.
- Each call in the Tokyo and Los Angeles checks ran in a fresh process, which confirms state persists across restarts.
- A leftover lock from a dead process was cleared, and the next three calls gave allow, allow, deny.

I did not test a lock that is stale only by age (30 seconds or more) with its owner process still alive. History older than 7 days is dropped on write.
